assertion.statement: The actual sections J^2 q_i, already regular at every codimension-one point, extend uniquely across codimension two on the maximal stack.
assertion.objects: The regular Noetherian maximal D210 Deligne-Mumford stack and its invertible square-dualizing line with rational sections J^2 q0,J^2 q1.
assertion.hypotheses: The stack is regular and flat over the base. The line is invertible, the sections are regular on the generic fibre, and the separately proved vertical valuation bounds give regularity at vertical codimension-one points.
assertion.quantifiers: Both displayed sections, on every regular etale chart and every codimension-one point.
assertion.parameter_range: The actual maximal stack, including primes dividing210; no tame coarse quotient is assumed there.
assertion.uniformity: The same rational sections and line extend; no rescaling beyond the already fixed J^2.
assertion.constants: J remains2765952000; no new height constant.
assertion.normalizations: Trivialize the line on affine regular etale charts; apply the source with M=R, a free rank-one and hence reflexive module.
assertion.exceptional_cases: This does not construct a coarse-model line bundle, supply the valuation bounds, or extend a general nonreflexive sheaf.
assertion.limit_order: Choose an etale scheme atlas of the regular Noetherian Deligne-Mumford maximal stack and trivialize the invertible square-dualizing line on affine open charts. Each connected regular chart is a normal domain. The generic bicanonical section is regular at horizontal height-one primes; the separate vertical valuation calculation proves it at vertical height-one primes. Apply Tag0AVB with the free rank-one module, which is reflexive, to obtain a unique regular section on each chart. The extensions agree on etale overlaps because they agree on the dense generic fibre and the line is locally free on a reduced flat atlas. Descent for sections gives the unique section on the stack. No coarse-model pullback or tame argument at bad primes is used.

publication.title: Reflexive modules
publication.corrections: Exact retrieved HTML pin retained; only implication reflexive to height-one intersection is used.

available_assertion.statement: A finite reflexive module over a Noetherian normal domain is the intersection of its height-one localizations inside its generic fibre.
available_assertion.objects: A Noetherian normal domain R, its fraction field K and finite reflexive R-module M.
available_assertion.hypotheses: R is a Noetherian normal domain; M is finite and reflexive.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every such R and M, intersecting over all height-one prime ideals of R.
available_assertion.uniformity: No quantitative bound or choice of model is part of the assertion.
available_assertion.normalizations: The intersection is taken in M tensor_R K using the torsion-free embeddings.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: No statement is made for arbitrary nonnormal rings or nonreflexive modules.
available_assertion.limit_order: Take the height-one localizations of the fixed module inside its generic fibre.
